today.question_title: Maximize Spanning Tree Stability with Upgrades
hints_cache: This is a classic 'maximize the minimum' problem. Instead of trying to calculate the stability directly, try picking a potential stability value and checking if it is achievable.
Since the possible stability values are bounded by the edge strengths, you can use Binary Search to find the highest possible minimum strength that satisfies the constraints.
For a target stability 'X', every single edge you pick for your tree must have a strength of at least 'X'. This means any mandatory edge weaker than 'X' makes that target impossible immediately.

To check if 'X' is possible, use a Union-Find (DSU) structure. First, add all mandatory edges. Then, greedily add optional edges that are already at least 'X'. Finally, use your 'k' upgrades on any remaining edges that only reach 'X' after doubling.

The target 'X' is valid if: 1) Mandatory edges don't form cycles, 2) All mandatory edges are >= 'X', and 3) You can connect all nodes into one component using mandatory edges, free optional edges, and at most 'k' upgraded edges.
